newsitem.title: EU: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR FEB 17-DEC 31, 1997. (1 OF 2)
newsitem.headline: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR FEB 17-DEC 31, 1997. (1 OF 2)

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
AMSTERDAM - Dutch presidency hosts European Council of heads of state or government (June 16-17).
MADRID - NATO holds summit to set the course for enlargement (July 8 and 9).
LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg presidency hosts European Council of heads of state or government (December 12-13).
MONDAY, FEBRUARY 17
BRUSSELS - ECOFIN Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Preparation of stage 3 of EMU.
- Solvency ratio directive for credit institutions.
- (possibly) Taxation.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Farm Council (To February 18).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commission report on the tobacco market.
- (possibly) Presentation of the olive oil report.
- Identification of cattle and beef labelling - discussion and proposal.
- Portuguese request following the EU-U.S. Blair House agreement report on oil seeds.
- Proposal for veterinary equivalency agreement.
- Geographical identification of origin.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (To February 21).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Report on the conclusion by the EC of the Energy Charter Treaty charter and to the protocol on energy efficiency and related environmental aspects.
- Guido Podesta report on development problems and structural interventions in Italy.
- Gerhard Botz report on development problems and structural interventions in Germany for 1994-1999.
- Konstantinos Hatzidakis report on Commission communication on cohesion and environment policy.

AMSTERDAM (NEW ITEM) - Dutch EU presidency hosts experts meeting on public service broadcasting in Europe (To February 18). Main discussions focus on the role of public service broadcasting in the information society; public financing of public service broadcasting in relation to the treaty and EC competition policy; international cooperation between public service broadcasters. Venue: Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky. Contact: Andre Matthijse, Netherlands Broadcasting Corporation NOS (31) 35 677 37 87.

DOHA, Qatar (NEW ITEM) - Ministerial meeting and seventh joint council between the Gulf Cooperation Council and the EU. Participants include: Qatar Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad Bin Jaber Al-Thani, Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo and European Commissioner Marin. Discussions focus on the implementation of the cooperation agreement; free trade agreement negotiations; exchange of views on development in the two regions; exchange of views on political questions of common interest and approval of the joint declaration - followed by a closing news conference.
TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 18
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (second of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Ria Oomen-Ruijten report on the application of social security regimes to employees and their family members who move in the Community; consumer protection in unit pricing.
- Barbara Weiler report on social protection in Europe and on the future of social protection.
- Taminio recommendation on aids granted in rail, road and sea transport.
- James Janssen Van Raay report on investors compensation system.
- Evelyne Gebhardt report on recognition of diplomas.
- Ana Palacio Vallelersundi report on copyright.
- Lindholm report on the statute for EC civil servants and other agents on equal treatment between men and women.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Votes on reports under cooperation, codecision and assent procedures and on other motions for resolutions on which debate has closed.
- (1730/1630 GMT) Questions to the Commission.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Union for Europe holds press lunch (1300/1200 GMT). Venue: 76, Allee de la Robertsau. Contact: Union for Europe (33) 3 88 17 46 36.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - CERCAL (Centre for Study and Promotion of Relations between the Countries of the EC and of Latin America) holds seminar on "Civil society in Latin America: what relations with the European civil society". Venue: CERCAL, ULB Auditorium 1309. Contact: CERCAL (322) 650 3103.

AMSTERDAM (NEW ITEM) - Dutch EU presidency hosts experts meeting on public service broadcasting in Europe (second of two days). News conference on the outcome of the meeting at 1300/1200 GMT. Venue: Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky. Contact: Andre Matthijse, Netherlands Broadcasting Corporation NOS (31) 35 677 37 87.
WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 19
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (third of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Manuel Medina Ortega report on allegations of infringement or of bad administration on the application of Community law on BSE.
- Mihail Papayannakis report on labelling of beef meat and beef meat based products.
- Karl Erik Olsson report on the organisation of veterinary control on products from third countries entering the Community.
- Xaver Mayer report on beef identification and registration system.
- Philip Whitehead report on priorities for consumer policy.
- Elena Marinucci report on financial services: responding to consumer expectations.
- Joint debate on:
- Mosiek-Urbahn and Ernesto Caccavale joint report on the approximation of member states' legal, regulatory and administrative dispositions on consumer credit.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Votes on:
- Reports under cooperation, codecision and assent procedures; other motions for resolutions on which debate has closed.
- (1730/1630 GMT) Questions to the Council.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds conference on "Post-Papandreou Greece: new economic and foreign policy directions" (0900/0800 GMT). Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

LONDON - Agra Europe holds 16th annual European outlook '97 conference (0830/0830 GMT) (To February 20). Speakers include: British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg. Venue: The Landmark Hotel. Contact: Agra Europe (44) 1892 511 807.
THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 20
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (fourth of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Imelda Read report on the application of an open network to voice telephony and the establishment of a universal telecoms service in a competitive environment.
- Graham Mather report on the strengthening of an evaluation system on the impact on companies.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Votes on reports under cooperation, codecision and assent procedures and on other motions for resolutions on which debate has closed.
- (1500/1400 GMT) Debates on topical and urgent subjects of major importance - followed by votes.
- (1800/1700 GMT) Monica Stefania Baldi report on EU-ACP joint assembly in 1996.
- Michael McGowan report on complementarity between cooperation and development policy in the EU and those of member states.
- Raimondo Fassa report on links between emergency aid, rehabilitation and development.
FRIDAY, FEBRUARY 21
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (last of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Votes on procedures without report; votes on reports without debate; motions for resolutions on which debate has closed.
- Jan Mulder report on balancing of member state accounts on expenses financed by EAGGF, "Guarantee" section, for 1992 as well as certain expenses for 1993.
- Astrid Lulling report on spouses helping independent workers.
SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 22

LOUVAIN-LA-NEUVE - Leuven Catholic University (UCL) European Studies Institute holds conference on "European policy in Belgium" (0900/0800 GMT). Venue: UCL, Urbain Vaes Hall. Contact: European Studies Institute (3210) 47 85 50.
SUNDAY, FEBRUARY 23
BRUSSELS - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana meets Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov. The talks will centre on a permanent consultative mechanism between Moscow and the alliance.
MONDAY, FEBRUARY 24
BRUSSELS - General Affairs Council (To February 25). Palestinian President Yasser Arafat signs EU-Palestinian Authority interim association accord in margins of the Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Belarus: follow-up to fact-finding mission.
- Former Yugoslavia:
- Donor conference;
- Regional approach.
- Middle East peace process.
- Great Lakes region.
- Relations with South Africa: state of negotiations.
- European Monitoring Centre on racism and xenophobia.
- Mediterranean policy:
- Preparation and organisation of the 2nd Ministerial meeting of the Euro-Mediterranean Partnership (follow-up to Barcelona);
- Egypt: state of negotiations on an association agreement;
- Lebanon: state of negotiations on an association agreement.
- Yemen: adoption of negotiating directives for new cooperation agreement.
- Relations with Mexico: state of negotiations on an economic and cooperation agreement.
- Relations with Australia.
- Transatlantic relations: follow-up to U.S. and Canada action plans.
- Relations with Turkmenistan: decision to open negotiations on a partnership and cooperation agreement.
- Burma/Myanmar: suspension of GSP for industrial products (possibly).
- Laos and Cambodia: decisions to sign cooperation agreements (possible A items).
- Trade questions:
- Draft Council report to European Council on the evolution of the trade policies and preferential agreements of the Community;
- State of negotiations on an Information Technology Agreement.
- XIII San Jose Ministerial Conference: determination of the Union's position.
- Association Council with Slovakia: determination of the Union's position.
- Association Council with Bulgaria: determination of the Union's position.
- Association Council with Cyprus: determination of the Union's position.
- In the margins of the Council:
- Association Council with Slovakia;
- Association Council with Bulgaria;
- Association Council with Cyprus.
TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 25

BRUSSELS - The Euro-Arab Centre for Studies holds conference on "Euro-Arab relations: present and future" (0900/0800 GMT) (To February 27). Sessions include: the Euro-Arab dialogue; Euro-Arab political relations; relations and security; economic relations; commercial and financial relations; cultural relations; the Euro-Islamic dialogue; the European and Arab regional groups. Speakers include: European Commissioner Marin; UNESCO Director General Federico Mayor and Arab League States Secretary General Ahmad Ismat Abdel Meguid. Contact: The Euro-Arab Centre for Studies (33) 1 49 53 95 80.
WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 26
BRUSSELS - EU-San Jose meeting involving Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama.
BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (To February 27).

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "Finland's first two years of EU membership" (1315/1215 GMT). Speaker is Finland Permanent EU Representative Antti Satuli. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 27

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Quality Beef holds news conference (1100/1000 GMT). Main issues discussed: nutritional aspects and consumer issues; Community policy in the promotion of agricultural products. Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: Francine Robbens (322) 218 7241.

BRUSSELS - Cogen Europe holds conference on "Energy market liberalisation - What impact on the environment" (1430/1330 GMT). Speakers include: MEPs Ken Collins and W.G van Velzen. Venue: Renaissance Hotel. Contact: Cogen Europe (322) 772 8290.
FRIDAY, FEBRUARY 28
AMSTERDAM - Informal Development Council (To March 2). No agenda yet available.

COLOGNE, Germany (NEW ITEM) - ARD Westdeutscher Rundfunk hosts conference on the "Information society in Europe" (1000/0900 GMT). Speakers include: European Commissioner Bangemann and German Education, Science, Research Minister Juergen Ruettgers. Venue: WDR, Funkhaus Wallrafplatz. Contact: Stephan Piltz, WDR (49) 221 220 2405.

AMSTERDAM - Informal Education Council. No agenda yet available.

Contact: Energiesparverband (43) 732 6584 4380.

BRUSSELS - Inernational Accounting Standards Committee holds conference on "International accounting standards - Implications for major European corporations" (1000/0900 GMT) (To Maouchstone Exhibitions and Conferences (44) 181 332 0044.

SATURDAY, MARCH 15
